identificationModule.briefTitle: CHiR Therapy for Elderly DLBCL Intolerant to Chemo
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Single-arm, Multicenter, Prospective Clinical Study of CHiR (chidamide, Zanubrutinib, and Lenalidomide) for Newly Diagnosed MYC- and BCL2-positive Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) in Elderly Patients Intolerant to Chemotherapy.

leadSponsor.name: First Affiliated Hospital of Ningbo University

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The objective of exploring the application of CHiR is to evaluate its therapeutic efficacy and safety in newly diagnosed elderly patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) aged 70 and above, and to investigate the genetic subtypes that may benefit from CHiR. The primary endpoint is the complete remission rate (CRR) at the end of 8 cycles.

armGroups.label: CHiR
armGroups.description: The combined regimen of chidamide, zanubrutinib, and lenalidomide (CHiR) is employed to treat elderly patients with double-expressor lymphoma. This study aims to explore the efficacy and safety of this regimen in newly diagnosed elderly patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) who are intolerant to chemotherapy.

interventions.name: CHiR-DEL
interventions.description: Using the combined regimen of CHiR (chidamide, zanubrutinib, and lenalidomide) to treat newly diagnosed elderly patients with MYC- and BCL2-expressing positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) who are intolerant to chemotherapy.

primaryOutcomes.description: The primary endpoint is the complete remission rate (CRR) at the end of 8 cycles.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Each cycle consists of 21 days, with a total of 8 cycles.

locations.facility: The First Affiliated Hospital of Ningbo University
